title: Voice to coordinated work
subtitle: The implemented OpenWhispr, Orchestrator, and Brain system

nodes.label: Voice to coordinated work
nodes.summary: The OpenWhispr fork, agent team, and shared project memory form one inspectable workflow.
details: Click a branch to expand it, or follow a guided workflow. Select a component for evidence and cross-connections.
This is an implementation snapshot, not a live health monitor. Readiness limitations appear in component details.
The system uses local audio utilities and hosted reasoning providers. No local model was launched to build this map.

nodes.label: Speak and hear
nodes.summary: OpenWhispr turns speech into deliberate commands and dictation, then reads completed replies aloud.

nodes.label: Away access
nodes.summary: Phone voice and remote desktop use separate connections to the same Windows workstation.

nodes.label: Coordinate work
nodes.summary: One recorded lead coordinates bounded assignments, reviews outputs, and can transfer command.

nodes.label: Model providers
nodes.summary: Product names and model providers are shown together; the transport is separate from the role.

nodes.label: Create a team
nodes.summary: The lead chooses independent tasks, reserves capacity, starts workers, and integrates reviewed results.

nodes.label: Remember and recall
nodes.summary: A small SQLite knowledge graph stores reviewed facts, preferences, procedures, and useful episodes.

nodes.label: See what happened
nodes.summary: Dashboards expose activity, quota, memory receipts, evidence, and interactive conversations.

nodes.label: Keep control
nodes.summary: Explicit ownership, scope, review, resource limits, and deliberate controls keep the workflow bounded.

nodes.label: Home headset microphone
nodes.summary: Home uses the headset microphone.
details: Home uses the headset microphone. The latest saved microphone event used this input; that is not a direct reading of the saved profile selector.

nodes.label: Speech recognition
nodes.summary: Converts audio into recognized text, including deliberate command words.
details: Converts audio into recognized text, including deliberate command words. The current configured route is Nemotron streaming. Existing local speech components were inspected, not started by this audit.

nodes.label: Deliberate spoken commands
nodes.summary: Select the target, switch Home/Away, ask where text is going, pause/resume, finish dictation, or control readback.
details: Select the target, switch Home/Away, ask where text is going, pause/resume, finish dictation, or control readback. Command recognition starts from recognized speech, before cleanup.

nodes.label: Dictation cleanup
nodes.summary: Optional selected cleanup model improves grammar and readability.
details: Optional selected cleanup model improves grammar and readability. The saved local selection is Gemma. Cleanup is a different stage from speech recognition and Piper.

nodes.label: Guarded composer targeting
nodes.summary: Finds the selected editor's matching agent composer, confirms focus, and pastes/submits according to the selected target.
details: Finds the selected editor's matching agent composer, confirms focus, and pastes/submits according to the selected target. Target selection is independent from readback conversation selection.

nodes.label: Codex / ASTRA conversation
nodes.summary: A supported selected destination for voice input.
details: A supported selected destination for voice input. Final replies are observed from local Codex completion events. Opening a conversation alone does not change OpenWhispr's target.

nodes.label: Claude Code / Fable conversation
nodes.summary: A supported selected destination for voice input.
details: A supported selected destination for voice input. An installed Stop hook forwards a completed reply to the authenticated local readback bridge.

nodes.label: Completed-reply events
nodes.summary: Codex completion watcher and Claude Stop hook feed the readback path.
details: Codex completion watcher and Claude Stop hook feed the readback path. Worker/tool progress is not the intended spoken channel. Google/Grok results can be summarized by the lead first.

nodes.label: Reply inbox and playback queue
nodes.summary: Stores pending replies, selects a readback conversation, and offers Replay/Skip.
details: Stores pending replies, selects a readback conversation, and offers Replay/Skip. Playback waits for microphone-safe conditions; pauses and disabled readback preserve unread work.

nodes.label: Piper spoken answers
nodes.summary: Prepares and length-bounds final reply text, synthesizes speech, and sends it to the configured output.
details: Prepares and length-bounds final reply text, synthesizes speech, and sends it to the configured output. Piper-only assets are installed; automatic SAPI fallback is disabled.

nodes.label: Voicemeeter audio routing
nodes.summary: Receives Piper audio and routes it to the local headset and/or a separate return bus for the phone call.
details: Receives Piper audio and routes it to the local headset and/or a separate return bus for the phone call. Running process and a healthy virtual audio device were observed; bus routing was not live-tested.

nodes.label: Home headset playback
nodes.summary: The hardware output bus delivers spoken replies to the local headset when configured.
details: The hardware output bus delivers spoken replies to the local headset when configured.

nodes.label: Hands Free dashboard
nodes.summary: Shows the selected target, processing state, transcription/cleanup/paste-send durations, and readback inbox.
details: Shows the selected target, processing state, transcription/cleanup/paste-send durations, and readback inbox. Paste/send timing is not remote-delivery confirmation.

nodes.label: Phone microphone and headphones
nodes.summary: A private Discord call carries speech from the phone and spoken answers back to its headphones.
details: A private Discord call carries speech from the phone and spoken answers back to its headphones. A call must already be connected; OpenWhispr does not create or maintain it.

nodes.label: Private Discord voice call
nodes.summary: Transports phone audio to PC playback and takes the independent Voicemeeter return as PC microphone audio.
details: Transports phone audio to PC playback and takes the independent Voicemeeter return as PC microphone audio. This route is separate from approved text DM controls and from RustDesk remote desktop.

nodes.label: Virtual cable / Away microphone
nodes.summary: Discord plays incoming speech into CABLE Input; CABLE Output becomes the OpenWhispr Away microphone.
details: Discord plays incoming speech into CABLE Input; CABLE Output becomes the OpenWhispr Away microphone. The return path must not feed this same incoming cable.

nodes.label: Tailscale private network
nodes.summary: The installed private-network service is running and supports the configured remote-desktop path.
details: The installed private-network service is running and supports the configured remote-desktop path. Current phone reachability was not tested.
Read-only host service check; no identifiers collected into the map.

nodes.label: RustDesk desktop control
nodes.summary: Installed remote desktop route; the host was not running during this audit.
details: Installed host component for seeing and controlling the Windows desktop over the private network. It is not the voice transport. Current RustDesk process/service was not running or not observed; the Docker engine for the configured self-hosted server was unavailable.
Installed, current remote session unavailable/unverified
Read-only installation/process check; current live connection not claimed.

nodes.label: One active orchestrator
nodes.summary: ASTRA is the default lead; an explicit claim can make Fable the lead.
details: The coordinator record binds owner, session, and generation. Worker messages do not transfer leadership.

nodes.label: Durable project checkpoint
nodes.summary: Objective, decisions, completed work, next steps, jobs, and approvals survive a handoff.
details: A stable workspace project ID keeps new runs in the same memory project.

nodes.label: 5% command-driven handoff
nodes.summary: At work milestones the current lead can prepare and launch the low-usage transfer.
details: The configured threshold is 5% remaining. This check is run by the lead at milestones.
Fable claims command explicitly. The outgoing lead remains available as a bounded worker while its allowance permits.

nodes.label: Review and integration
nodes.summary: The lead checks returned work against files, tests, and acceptance criteria.
details: Execution success and review acceptance are separate states. Acceptance can trigger memory capture.

nodes.label: ASTRA / Codex / OpenAI
nodes.summary: The Codex session can lead and create native worker sessions.
details: This run used the native collaboration tools. ASTRA is the configured role name, not a separate provider.

nodes.label: Fable / Claude / Anthropic
nodes.summary: Claude Code supplies the Fable coordinator and the hosted Claude worker route.
details: An interactive coordinator session supports attachment. Supplied-text worker tasks use separate canonical task records.
Fable and Claude refer to the same provider family here.

nodes.label: Gemini / Google / Antigravity
nodes.summary: The guarded Antigravity CLI route returns supplied-text work for review.
details: The dispatcher verifies the pinned executable and deny-hook boundary, reserves allowance, and validates the returned stream.
The retired Gemini consumer CLI route is excluded.

nodes.label: Grok / xAI / Grok Build
nodes.summary: The installed Grok worker transport accepts a bounded supplied-text assignment.
details: Availability and remaining allowance are checked separately from a route being implemented.

nodes.label: Task-based team sizing
nodes.summary: Plan independent workstreams and reserve review capacity before creating workers.
details: The team command uses task type, independent workstreams, quota, and retained timing evidence.
Its proposed team is advisory; it is not a universal scheduler or experimentally proven optimum.

nodes.label: Native worker sessions
nodes.summary: The lead creates bounded native Codex assignments through the collaboration tools.
details: Each worker receives a scoped prompt and explicit file ownership. The lead includes relevant recalled memory explicitly.
Workers report back for review; native creation does not pass through the supplied-text dispatcher.

nodes.label: Concurrency and waves
nodes.summary: This native host supports 4 active agents total: 1 lead plus 3 workers.
details: A 6-10-assignment team must use waves under this host limit.
The application planner defaults to a cap of 4 workers excluding the lead; use cap 3 for this native session.
External provider tasks have separate quota, admission, and transport constraints; there is no verified universal 10-bot concurrency guarantee.

nodes.label: Bounded worker assignment
nodes.summary: An explicit task, project scope, input, size, and output contract define each dispatch.
details: Default memory recall uses the scoped task label. An explicit query can refine it; --no-memory disables it.
Native worker prompts are composed by the lead; the supplied-text dispatcher is a different route.

nodes.label: Usage reservation
nodes.summary: Read quota and reserve task capacity before asking a provider to execute.
details: Uncertain usage is not treated as free. Unresolved executions retain reconciliation state.

nodes.label: Execution and deadlines
nodes.summary: Worker execution records phases, deadlines, output, and failures.
details: Hosted deadlines use task-size defaults with an explicit bounded override. Native session pauses have no dispatcher-enforced deadline.

nodes.label: Canonical task and review
nodes.summary: A durable task result separates execution, review acceptance, and memory capture.
details: A reviewed closeout may be imported without running a provider. Such artifacts are marked and excluded from worker timing comparisons.

nodes.label: Local knowledge store
nodes.summary: SQLite and full-text search keep reviewed knowledge small and searchable.
details: Facts, preferences, procedures, and problem/solution episodes are separate memory types.
This is an explicit knowledge graph with retrieval, not a trained neural network. Graphiti is not installed.

nodes.label: Reviewed atomic capture
nodes.summary: One accepted closeout can save 1-24 concise memories and up to 64 justified links.
details: The reviewer supplies the lasting insights and relationship reasons. Capture does not run a model to guess them.
The transaction rolls back on invalid scope or capacity. A durable receipt prevents retry duplicates and resurrection after Forget.

nodes.label: Automatic accepted-task episode
nodes.summary: Accepting a scoped canonical task saves compact review evidence automatically.
details: Without a curated bundle, the default stores one compact episode. It does not attempt a semantic summary of every conversation.
A checkpoint alone is not a reviewed canonical task. Native work can use the explicit reviewed-closeout capture command.

nodes.label: Evidence-backed connections
nodes.summary: Directed typed links connect related knowledge within the same project and user.
details: Curated links include a short explanation visible in memory details. Each bundle link includes at least one newly captured node.
The graph is not forced to be fully connected. Unrelated memories can stand alone.

nodes.label: Bounded project recall
nodes.summary: Search ranks current approved knowledge and follows a small number of graph hops.
details: Keyword/alias relevance, importance, and age influence ordering. Source validity is rechecked.
The default returns at most 6 memories within 8,000 characters and one graph hop; the supported hop ceiling is two.

nodes.label: Memory in worker input
nodes.summary: Scoped supplied-text dispatch automatically retrieves context before execution.
details: The task retains memory IDs, scope, a context fingerprint, lookup timing, and whether execution was requested with that context.
Fallback preparation checks sources again. A receipt proves requested input, not that a provider read or relied on it.

nodes.label: Review, replace, forget
nodes.summary: Approval and validity determine recall; supersession and Forget retire knowledge.
details: Proposals stay out of recall. Forget removes memory content and derived search/graph data while retaining bounded change tombstones.
Review evidence remains attached to task-sourced knowledge.

nodes.label: Orchestrator viewer
nodes.summary: See the selected run, recorded lead conversation, worker phases, and activity timestamps.
details: Native activity uses saved session evidence where linked; historical records can lack timings.

nodes.label: Open interactive console
nodes.summary: Open the exact existing Codex conversation or attach to the live Fable console.
details: The button depends on a valid matching session binding and available attachment route.
ASTRA opens the saved Codex conversation in VS Code. Fable attaches the matching Claude daemon console.
The viewer is observational; the opened conversation or console is interactive.

nodes.label: Brain dashboard
nodes.summary: Browse memories, links, review history, storage, recall, and task memory-use receipts.
details: Stable project/run links connect it to the Orchestrator viewer.
Normal polling is quiet: Brain checks every 10 seconds and the viewer every 5 seconds. Retry or Apply pending updates appears only when needed.

nodes.label: Explicit usefulness review
nodes.summary: A reviewer can rate supplied memory as helped, neutral, or harmful after accepting the answer.
details: Feedback is bound to the accepted answer and exact requested memory context. Changed evidence makes old feedback stale.
Dashboard counts describe a bounded retained sample, not lifetime performance or causal improvement.

nodes.label: Provider usage view
nodes.summary: Provider observations show remaining allowance and collection status.
details: An unknown or stale reading remains visible as such. An observation is not a promise of future capacity.

nodes.label: Source and scope checks
nodes.summary: Project/user boundaries, source fingerprints, named reviews, and owner identity are checked.
details: Memory is evidence; it does not grant permission, authorize exports, or change leadership.

nodes.label: Storage and retention limits
nodes.summary: 10,000 memories, 30,000 relationships, a 256 MiB database, and bounded task/trace storage.
details: Brain admission budget is 1 GiB; total managed application admission budget is 2 GiB. These do not limit unrelated programs or the entire SSD.
The recall trace ring retains 200 records and the change feed 1,000 entries. The graph view displays a bounded recent snapshot.

nodes.label: Deliberate user control
nodes.summary: Voice commands choose destinations; saved approvals and the interactive console expose control points.
details: External nonpublic exports require their authorized scope. Existing authorization is retained in the run checkpoint.

edges.label: Stop hook to authenticated local bridge
Private remote-desktop connection when services are ready
Uses exact project and task query
Desktop access when host is ready

journeys.label: Speak and hear
journeys.summary: A deliberate dictation reaches the chosen lead conversation; completed replies return through Piper.

journeys.label: Use it away from home
journeys.summary: A connected Discord call carries speech in and an independent audio bus carries replies out. Remote desktop is a separate optional path.

journeys.label: Dispatch hosted work
journeys.summary: The lead plans work, respects capacity, supplies memory, reserves allowance, and reviews the result.

journeys.label: Learn from completed work
journeys.summary: Reviewed knowledge becomes atomic memories and justified links; later work retrieves it and retains an inspectable use receipt.
